html:
Special police force of masterless samurai that served the Tokugawa shogunate in Kyoto from 1863 until 1869.

It began in 1863 as a group of rough swordsmen, many from outside the samurai class by birth, hired to guard the shogun's visit to Kyoto. The city was full of assassins who wanted to expel foreigners and restore imperial rule. The group stayed on under the lord of Aizu, who was the shogunate's protector of Kyoto. Its leaders were Kondo Isami, Hijikata Toshizo and, early on, Serizawa Kamo, who was purged in 1863. They had a strict code, and breaking it could mean ordering the death of a member.

Its best-known deed was the Ikedaya raid in 1864. After the shogunate lost the war of 1868 to 1869, the group fought on. Kondo was executed in 1868, and Hijikata died in the Battle of Hakodate in 1869.

The Shinsengumi are loved in Japanese film, manga and novels as the last loyal swordsmen of the old order, before the Meiji Restoration.
sum: Special police force of masterless samurai that served the Tokugawa shogunate in Kyoto from 1863 until 1869.
